passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this song.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He wanted it sung to the tune called “Lilies.”

passages.text: Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He said to use the tune called “Lilies.”
David prayed to God.
He said, “Save me, O God.”
He said, “The waters have come up to my neck.”
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ עַֽל־ שׁוֹשַׁנִּ֬ים לְדָוִֽד׃ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֤י בָ֖אוּ מַ֣יִם עַד־ נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: I have sunk into the miry depths, where there is no footing; I have drifted into deep waters, where the flood engulfs me.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David feels overwhelmed.
David says, “I have sunk into deep mud.”
There is no solid ground for David.
David has entered deep waters.
A strong flood covers David.
passages.original: טָבַ֤עְתִּי׀ בִּיוֵ֣ן מְ֭צוּלָה וְאֵ֣ין מָעֳמָ֑ד בָּ֥אתִי בְמַעֲמַקֵּי־ מַ֝֗יִם וְשִׁבֹּ֥לֶת שְׁטָפָֽתְנִי׃

passages.text: I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David feels very tired from crying.
His throat is dry.
His eyes grow weak.
He looks for God.
passages.original: יָגַ֣עְתִּי בְקָרְאִי֮ נִחַ֪ר גְּר֫וֹנִ֥י כָּל֥וּ עֵינַ֑י מְ֝יַחֵ֗ל לֵאלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are those who would destroy me— my enemies for no reason. Though I did not steal, I must repay.
passages.sermon:
Many people hate me for no reason.
They outnumber the hairs on my head.
Many people want to destroy me.
My enemies accuse me falsely.
They attack me without cause.
I did not steal anything.
But I must repay as if I did.
passages.original: רַבּ֤וּ׀ מִשַּׂעֲר֣וֹת רֹאשִׁי֮ שֹׂנְאַ֪י חִ֫נָּ֥ם עָצְמ֣וּ מַ֭צְמִיתַי אֹיְבַ֣י שֶׁ֑קֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ גָ֝זַ֗לְתִּי אָ֣ז אָשִֽׁיב׃

passages.text: You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You.
passages.sermon: God, You know my foolishness.\r\nYou see all my guilt.\r\nNothing I have done is hidden from You.
passages.original: אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים אַתָּ֣ה יָ֭דַעְתָּ לְאִוַּלְתִּ֑י וְ֝אַשְׁמוֹתַ֗י מִמְּךָ֥ לֹא־ נִכְחָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me, O Lord GOD of Hosts; may those who seek You not be dishonored through me, O God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God of Hosts.
The Lord is the God of Israel.
Some people hope in the Lord.
Some people seek the Lord.
I pray that people who hope in the Lord will not be ashamed because of me.
I pray that people who seek the Lord will not be dishonored because of me.
passages.original: אַל־ יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ בִ֨י׀ קֹוֶיךָ֮ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֗ה צְבָ֫א֥וֹת אַל־ יִכָּ֣לְמוּ בִ֣י מְבַקְשֶׁ֑יךָ אֱ֝לֹהֵ֗י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For I have endured scorn for Your sake, and shame has covered my face.
passages.sermon:
I am speaking to God.
I have suffered scorn because of You.
I have carried this disgrace for Your sake.
Shame has covered my face.
People have dishonored me because I follow You.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָ֭לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֣אתִי חֶרְפָּ֑ה כִּסְּתָ֖ה כְלִמָּ֣ה פָנָֽי׃

passages.text: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons, because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a servant of God.
He has become a stranger to his brothers.
He is like a foreigner to his mother’s sons.
Zeal for God’s house has consumed him.
Insults meant for God have fallen on him.
passages.original: מ֭וּזָר הָיִ֣יתִי לְאֶחָ֑י וְ֝נָכְרִ֗י לִבְנֵ֥י אִמִּֽי׃ כִּֽי־ קִנְאַ֣ת בֵּיתְךָ֣ אֲכָלָ֑תְנִי וְחֶרְפּ֥וֹת ח֝וֹרְפֶ֗יךָ נָפְל֥וּ עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: I wept and fasted, but it brought me reproach.
passages.sermon:
I wept.
I fasted.
People saw my weeping and fasting.
They gave me reproach because of it.
passages.original: וָאֶבְכֶּ֣ה בַצּ֣וֹם נַפְשִׁ֑י וַתְּהִ֖י לַחֲרָפ֣וֹת לִֽי׃

passages.text: I made sackcloth my clothing, and I was sport to them.
passages.sermon:
I put on sackcloth as my clothing.
I wore sackcloth to show my sorrow and humility.
The people saw me in sackcloth.
They made me into a joke.
They used me as an example of ridicule.
passages.original: וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לְבוּשִׁ֣י שָׂ֑ק וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמָשָֽׁל׃

passages.text: Those who sit at the gate mock me, and I am the song of drunkards.
passages.sermon:
People sit at the city gate.
These people talk about me.
They mock me.
Drunk people sing about me.
They make me the subject of their songs.
passages.original: יָשִׂ֣יחוּ בִ֭י יֹ֣שְׁבֵי שָׁ֑עַר וּ֝נְגִינ֗וֹת שׁוֹתֵ֥י שֵׁכָֽר׃

passages.text: But my prayer to You, O LORD, is for a time of favor. In Your abundant loving devotion, O God, answer me with Your sure salvation.
passages.sermon:
I pray to You, LORD.
I pray at a time when You show favor.
You are God.
You have great loving devotion.
Answer me, O God.
Save me with Your true salvation.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י תְפִלָּתִֽי־ לְךָ֨׀ יְהוָ֡ה עֵ֤ת רָצ֗וֹן אֱלֹהִ֥ים בְּרָב־ חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝נֵ֗נִי בֶּאֱמֶ֥ת יִשְׁעֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Rescue me from the mire and do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and out of the deep waters.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to God.
The psalmist asks God to rescue him from the mire.
The mire is deep mud or trouble.
The psalmist asks God not to let him sink.
The psalmist asks God to deliver him from his enemies.
The psalmist asks God to save him from deep waters.
The deep waters represent overwhelming danger or distress.
passages.original: הַצִּילֵ֣נִי מִ֭טִּיט וְאַל־ אֶטְבָּ֑עָה אִנָּצְלָ֥ה מִ֝שֹּֽׂנְאַ֗י וּמִמַּֽעֲמַקֵּי־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Do not let the floods engulf me or the depths swallow me up; let not the Pit close its mouth over me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker prays to the LORD for help.
The speaker asks God to protect him from danger.
He says, "Do not let the floods cover me."
He says, "Do not let the deep waters swallow me."
He says, "Do not let the Pit close its mouth over me."
passages.original: אַל־ תִּשְׁטְפֵ֤נִי׀ שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת מַ֭יִם וְאַל־ תִּבְלָעֵ֣נִי מְצוּלָ֑ה וְאַל־ תֶּאְטַר־ עָלַ֖י בְּאֵ֣ר פִּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Answer me, O LORD, for Your loving devotion is good; turn to me in keeping with Your great compassion.
passages.sermon:
The speaker calls to the LORD.
The LORD is God.
The speaker asks God to answer him.
God’s loving devotion is good.
God has great compassion.
The speaker asks God to turn to him.
The speaker wants God to act because of God’s goodness and compassion.
passages.original: עֲנֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה כִּי־ ט֣וֹב חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ פְּנֵ֣ה אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly!
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a servant of the LORD.
The servant feels distress.
The servant asks the LORD not to hide His face.
The servant asks the LORD to answer quickly.
passages.original: וְאַל־ תַּסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵֽעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּֽי־ צַר־ לִ֝֗י מַהֵ֥ר עֲנֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Draw near to my soul and redeem me; ransom me because of my foes.
passages.sermon:
God, I am in trouble.
\r\nMy enemies surround me.
\r\nCome close to me.
\r\nSave my soul.
\r\nRescue me from my enemies.
passages.original: קָרְבָ֣ה אֶל־ נַפְשִׁ֣י גְאָלָ֑הּ לְמַ֖עַן אֹיְבַ֣י פְּדֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: You know my reproach, my shame and disgrace. All my adversaries are before You.
passages.sermon:
God, You know my reproach.
You know my shame.
You know my disgrace.
All my adversaries stand before You.
You see every enemy I have.
You know all that I suffer from them.
passages.original: אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֗עְתָּ חֶרְפָּתִ֣י וּ֭בָשְׁתִּי וּכְלִמָּתִ֑י נֶ֝גְדְּךָ֗ כָּל־ צוֹרְרָֽי׃

passages.text: Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering.
Insults have broken the speaker’s heart.
The speaker feels deep despair.
The speaker hoped someone would show sympathy.
No one showed sympathy.
The speaker searched for comforters.
The speaker found no comforters.
passages.original: חֶרְפָּ֤ה׀ שָֽׁבְרָ֥ה לִבִּ֗י וָֽאָ֫נ֥וּשָׁה וָאֲקַוֶּ֣ה לָנ֣וּד וָאַ֑יִן וְ֝לַמְנַחֲמִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א מָצָֽאתִי׃

passages.text: They poisoned my food with gall and gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.
passages.sermon:
My enemies gave me gall when I was hungry.
They put poison in my food.
When I was thirsty, they gave me vinegar to drink.
They did not give me water.
They tried to harm me instead of helping me.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ בְּבָרוּתִ֣י רֹ֑אשׁ וְ֝לִצְמָאִ֗י יַשְׁק֥וּנִי חֹֽמֶץ׃

passages.text: May their table become a snare; may it be a retribution and a trap.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his enemies.
He asks God to punish them.
He says, "Let their table become a snare before them."
He means, "Let what should bring them peace become a trap."
He wants their blessings to turn into danger.
He wants their safety to become a cause for harm.
passages.original: יְהִֽי־ שֻׁלְחָנָ֣ם לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם לְפָ֑ח וְלִשְׁלוֹמִ֥ים לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.
passages.sermon:
Their eyes will become dark.
They will not see.
Their backs will always be bent.
They will stumble forever.
passages.original: תֶּחְשַׁ֣כְנָה עֵ֭ינֵיהֶם מֵרְא֑וֹת וּ֝מָתְנֵ֗יהֶם תָּמִ֥יד הַמְעַֽד׃

passages.text: Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.
passages.sermon:
God, You have anger.
God, You have burning wrath.
Pour out Your anger on them.
Let Your burning wrath reach them.
Let Your anger overtake them.
passages.original: שְׁפָךְ־ עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם זַעְמֶ֑ךָ וַחֲר֥וֹן אַ֝פְּךָ֗ יַשִּׂיגֵֽם׃

passages.text: May their place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in their tents.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist prays against his enemies.
He asks God to make their place empty.
He wants their home to be deserted.
He asks that no one will live in their tents.
passages.original: תְּהִי־ טִֽירָתָ֥ם נְשַׁמָּ֑ה בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם אַל־ יְהִ֥י יֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: For they persecute the one You struck and recount the pain of those You wounded.
passages.sermon:
God, You struck someone.
They persecute that person.
You wounded others.
They talk about the pain of those You wounded.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־ הִכִּ֣יתָ רָדָ֑פוּ וְאֶל־ מַכְא֖וֹב חֲלָלֶ֣יךָ יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Add iniquity to their iniquity; let them not share in Your righteousness.
passages.sermon:
God, you see their sin.
Add more sin to what they have already done.
Do not let them join in your righteousness.
Do not let them share in your goodness.
passages.original: תְּֽנָה־ עָ֭וֺן עַל־ עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְאַל־ יָ֝בֹ֗אוּ בְּצִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: May they be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous.
passages.sermon:
God keeps a Book of Life.
This book lists those who have life and favor from God.
The speaker asks God to remove certain people from this book.
He asks that God blot out their names.
He asks that God not write their names with the righteous.
These people will not be counted among the righteous.
passages.original: יִ֭מָּחֽוּ מִסֵּ֣פֶר חַיִּ֑ים וְעִ֥ם צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים אַל־ יִכָּתֵֽבוּ׃

passages.text: But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God.
passages.sermon:
I am suffering.
I am in pain.
I feel distress.
God, I need Your help.
Let Your salvation protect me.
You, O God, can lift me up.
passages.original: וַ֭אֲנִי עָנִ֣י וְכוֹאֵ֑ב יְשׁוּעָתְךָ֖ אֱלֹהִ֣ים תְּשַׂגְּבֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: I will praise God’s name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving.
passages.sermon: I will praise God's name in song.\r\nI will exalt God with thanksgiving.
passages.original: אֲהַֽלְלָ֣ה שֵׁם־ אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּשִׁ֑יר וַאֲגַדְּלֶ֥נּוּ בְתוֹדָֽה׃

passages.text: And this will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
passages.sermon: This act will please the LORD.\r\nIt will please Him more than an ox.\r\nIt will please Him more than a bull with horns and hooves.
passages.original: וְתִיטַ֣ב לַֽ֭יהוָה מִשּׁ֥וֹר פָּ֗ר מַקְרִ֥ן מַפְרִֽיס׃

passages.text: The humble will see and rejoice. You who seek God, let your hearts be revived!
passages.sermon:
The humble people will see this.
The humble people will rejoice.
People who seek God, listen.
Let your hearts be revived.
passages.original: רָא֣וּ עֲנָוִ֣ים יִשְׂמָ֑חוּ דֹּרְשֵׁ֥י אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים וִיחִ֥י לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people.
passages.sermon: The LORD listens to the needy.\r\nThe LORD does not despise His captive people.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שֹׁמֵ֣עַ אֶל־ אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־ אֲ֝סִירָ֗יו לֹ֣א בָזָֽה׃

passages.text: Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
passages.sermon:
Heaven must praise God.
Earth must praise God.
The seas must praise God.
Everything that moves in the seas must praise God.
passages.original: יְֽ֭הַלְלוּהוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֑רֶץ יַ֝מִּ֗ים וְֽכָל־ רֹמֵ֥שׂ בָּֽם׃

passages.text: For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it.
passages.sermon:
God will save Zion.
God will rebuild the cities of Judah.
The people will live there.
The people will possess the land.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ י֘וֹשִׁ֤יעַ צִיּ֗וֹן וְ֭יִבְנֶה עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ שָׁ֝֗ם וִירֵשֽׁוּהָ׃

passages.text: The descendants of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His name will settle in it.
passages.sermon:
God has servants.
God gives His servants descendants.
The descendants of God's servants will inherit the land.
Some people love God's name.
Those who love God's name will live in the land.
passages.original: וְזֶ֣רַע עֲ֭בָדָיו יִנְחָל֑וּהָ וְאֹהֲבֵ֥י שְׁ֝מ֗וֹ יִשְׁכְּנוּ־ בָֽהּ׃
